By way of this Regular First Appeal, the State has assailed the award passed by learned Reference Court in Land Reference No.42S/4 of 2013, titled as Sh. Keshab Ram & another vs. Collector Land Acquisition, HPPWD, Sought Zone, WinterField, Shimla, H.P. & another, in terms whereof the Reference preferred by of the land owners under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was answered by the learned Court below in the following terms: rt " 19.

sentences.text: Taking into account my findings on issues No. 1 and 2 above, the reference petition succeeds and the same is allowed.
The petitioners are held entitled to the enhanced market value of the land at the rate of Rs.1627.44 per centiyar for all categories of the acquired land.

In addition to the said market value of the land, they will be entitled to an amount calculated at the rate of 12% per annum on the enhanced market value for the period commencing from the date of publication of the notification under Section 4 of the Act (01.08.2015) to the date of Collector's Award dated 29.09.2008, under Section 23(1A) of the Act.
They will also be entitled to a sum equivalent to 30% of the aforesaid market value of the land, in consideration of the compulsory nature of acquisition under Section 23 (2) of the Act.

In addition to that, the petitioners shall be entitled to interest on the sum awarded by this Court as compensation,
in excess of the sum awarded by the Collector as compensation, at the rate of 9% per annum for the 1 st year, that is, w.e.f.
.
Collector Land Acquisition Collector vs Sh. Keshab Ram & Another on 9 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154454982/
2 29.09.2008 i.e. the date of Award and at the rate of 15% per annum for the remaining period i.e.
w.e.f. 29.09.2009 to the date of deposit of enhanced compensation in the Court.
It is made clear that the amounts, if any, already awarded to the petitioners under Sections 23(1A) and 23 (2) of the Act shall be of deducted from the enhanced compensation payable.
20. The cost of petition is assessed as Rs. 2,000/ to be paid by the respondents."
2. rt The CrossObjections have also been filed by the land owners.

3. At this stage, the Court stands apprised that similar awards passed by learned Reference Court,
stood challenged by way of appeals by the State before this Court, in which the land owners had filed crossobjections for enhancement of the compensation.

The appeals stand disposed of by this Court in terms of the directions passed in RFA No.112 of 2016 a/w Cross Objections No.43 of 2017, titled State of H.P. & others vs. Durga Nand & others, as well as in RFA No.113 of 2016 a/w Cross Objections No.25 of 2017, titled as State of H.P. & others vs. Subhash Chand and others, decided on 07.07.2019.

sentences.text: Paras 8 to 12 of RFA Nos.112 and 113 of 2016 (supra) are as under:rt

" 8. Mr.Sanjeev Sood,
learned Additional Advocate General, representing the appellantsState, while fairly acknowledging the factum with regard to passing of judgment dated 12.10.2018 in Narayan Singh's case (supra),
conceded that claimants in the cases at hand are also entitled to enhanced market value of acquired land at the rate of Rs.2700/ per centiare alongwith all consequential statutory benefits as per the said judgment.

9. At this stage, it may be noticed that, ClaimantsCross Objectors have filed Cross Objections bearing C.O.Nos.43 & 25 of 2017 in RFA Nos.112 & 113 of 2016 respectively under Order 41 Rule 22 CPC praying therein for enhancement of compensation of award amount passed by learned District Judge (Forest) qua the acquired land.

10. Since this Court has held the claimants entitled for enhanced market value of acquired land at the rate of Rs.2700/ per centiare alongwith consequential statutory benefits, instead of Rs.1627.44,
in view of judgment .

rendered by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in Narayan Singh's case (supra), Mr.Sanjeev Sood,
learned Additional Advocate General, fairly conceded that cross objectorsclaimants (in C.O.
Nos.43 & 25 of 2017 in RFA Nos.112 & 113 of 2016 respectively) are also entitled to similar enhancement of compensation i.e. Rs.2700/ per of centiare alongwith consequential statutory benefits qua their acquired land as per their share.

11. Mr.B.S. Chauhan, learned Senior Counsel rt representing claimantscross objectors, also acceded to the market value of the land determined by a Co ordinate Bench of this Court in Narayan Singh's case (supra), and, accordingly, it is ordered that directions contained in Narayan Singh's case supra, shall mutatis mutandis apply to the case of claimantscross objectors also.

12. Consequently, in view of detailed discussion made hereinabove as well as fair stand adopted by Mr.Sanjeev Sood, learned Additional Advocate General representing the appellantsState, both the appeals bearing RFA Nos.112 & 113 of 2016 are dismissed.

The Cross Objections bearing C.O. Nos.43 & 25 of 2017 in RFA Nos.112 & 113 of 2016 respectively are allowed and it is ordered that directions contained in RFA No. 368 of 2014, titled: The Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited and Another vs. Narayan Singh and Others case supra shall mutatis mutandis apply in RFA Nos.112 &
113 of 2016 alongwith Cross Objection Nos.43 and 25 of .
2017 respectively."
7. Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, also stand disposed of. Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
